newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end up, next target seen 1,100.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end up, next target seen 1,100.

text.p: Austrian shares ended slightly firmer on Friday in line with international markets on slim turnover, with further gains seen next week, traders said.
"The target for the near future is 1,100," said one trader. Another saw the index in a range of 1,070 to 1,095 points over the forthcoming week.
The expiry of futures and options went smoothly, they noted. The November contract expired four points higher at 1,089.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips climbed 2.65 points or 0.24 percent to 1,087.55. Among its constituents 14 shares rose and seven fell.
The session's leading gainer was AMS, adding 2.82 percent to 730 schillings. "AMS has managed to find a good floor at 700," said one trader.

Preferred shares in Austria's flagship bank Creditanstalt were among the most actively traded, jumping seven schillings to 517. The deadline for bids for the government's 70 percent stake in the bank expires at midnight on Friday.
"Everyone is hoping this will finally be the end of the saga after six years," said a dealer about the bank's privatisation.
Vienna airport operator Flughafen was the leading decliner, shedding 1.88 percent to 523 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index inched up 0.52 points or 0.13 percent to 416.10.
